title: Remediation plan for quantized operator compatibility crash that triggered worker churn and model-flip
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A weekend incident where a converted int8 model introduced an unsupported fused-attention kernel led to persistent worker crash-loops on Dedicated pools. The crash caused autoscaler oscillation, capacity churn, and automatic routing to a hosted model variant which in turn produced measurable accuracy drift for a subset of customer prompts. This ticket captures the technical root cause, short-term mitigations we applied, and a prioritized remediation roadmap to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Duration: ~6 hours (2025-11-16 02:10 UTC to 2025-11-16 08:20 UTC). Affected: 3 Dedicated pools in us-west-2, ~0.4% of overall inference requests, 12 customer endpoints saw degraded outputs due to fallback to a lower-precision hosted variant. No sensitive data exposure. Visible customer complaints: 5 support incidents. Cost impact: increased autoscale churn and failed job retries estimated +$18k for the weekend.
root_cause: The quantization converter produced an operator lowering that selected a fused attention op variant (fused_attn_v2) not supported by the int8 kernel set on the target runtime image. Runtime attempted to JIT select a compatible kernel, hit an unsupported opcode, and raised SIGSEGV in the worker process. The worker kept restarting; autoscaler interpreted failures as capacity pressure and aggressively spawned new workers leading to capacity oscillation. Additionally, the fallback policy routed traffic to a hosted model version with a different dequant scale schedule, causing subtle distributional shift and accuracy drift for certain prompt templates.

2025-11-16 02:25 UTC - Autoscaler increased pool size; subsequent restarts caused further churn.
2025-11-16 03:01 UTC - Traffic routed to hosted fallback variant, engineering triage assembled.
2025-11-16 03:30 UTC - Hotfix: temporary route-exclusion for model bundle id m-bundle-2025-11-15 applied to stop traffic to failing workers.
2025-11-16 04:10 UTC - Hotpatch PR created to add converter preflight op-compat check (PR #5492).

2025-11-16 06:20 UTC - Autoscaler stabilization after route exclusion and manual pool scale-down.

short_term_mitigations: Applied immediate route exclusion for the failing model bundle to prevent new requests hitting crash-looping workers.
Throttled autoscaler to freeze addition of new GPU workers during triage window to avoid further oscillation.
Activated manual fallback policy override to a guarded hosted variant with explicit dequant scales and additional eval guards.
Rolled an emergency runtime image with an extra safety check that rejects unsupported opcodes at worker start (image runtime-2025.11.16-hotfix).
long_term_remediation: Integrate an operator compatibility manifest into the converter pipeline that emits a per-model supported-kernel matrix and fails conversion when required kernels are not present.
Add gated unit and integration tests for fused-attention lowering across quant levels (int8/int4) in the quant-converter repo.
Expand nightly canary suite to include real prompt evals for representative customer templates to detect subtle accuracy drift after fallback or conversion changes.
Improve autoscaler heuristics: add 'failure-rate' signal to prevent scale-ups triggered by worker crash loops.
Document a clear rollback & routing playbook for Dedicated pools including steps to safely exclude a model bundle and force traffic to pinned alternatives without triggering autoscaler spin-up.
